C01.why: Anomaly-spotting has a strong 'wait, was that there before?' hook and missed anomalies escalating into chases gives funny-scary failure, but the first 3 minutes are tap-chores and anomaly recognition decays into memorization once the 120-item deck is learned.
C01.fix: Kill the dead day phase: make day chores themselves the anomaly surface (a guest checks in twice, a key won't match) so the first 30 s already has a spot-the-difference beat, and add anomalies that actively bait wrong reports to keep spotting skill-based after memorization.

C02.why: KTANE's fun is frantic verbal description; collapsing it to an 8-icon wheel with strangers, a mandatory 3rd player and mid-round leavers turns the best part into a laggy charades bottleneck, though the ragdoll confetti failure is genuinely funny.
C02.fix: Design every rule page to be icon-native (Book's rules are expressed in the same stamps/symbols the wheel can send, so relaying is a fast tactile act, not translation) and add bot backfill for a dropped role so rounds never die.

C03.why: Instant, legible chaos and hilarious waterfall failures make the first minute great with anyone, but a single hold button gives each player almost no decisions and the novelty flattens after a few courses.
C03.fix: Give each seat a second contextual verb (bail water, bat away a croc, grab a floating coin, brace for impact) and let players hop seats mid-run so roles and priorities shift moment to moment.

C04.why: Inspect-and-judge is a real decision loop with tension (buy a fake vs. lose a treasure), but once a player learns the tell catalogue it becomes a checklist, and co-op split-inspection adds bookkeeping rather than fun; Forger Night is the most interesting part.
C04.fix: Make Forger Night (social deduction with physical tells) the headline mode and give NPC customers bluff/haggle behaviours plus a ticking queue so every judgement is a pressured gamble rather than a lookup.

C05.why: Breaking a house with physics is fun in second one with zero progression, the 60-second panic cleanup is a natural comedy peak, and sneaking evidence behind the Parent's back gives agency and betrayal that works with silent strangers; risk is a slow, lonely 3-minute inspection and a Parent role that is weaker fun than the kids'.
C05.fix: Cut inspection to ~90 s and give the Parent active tools (sniff trail, blacklight, 'freeze!' shout that catches anyone moving) so Parent is a hunter, not an auditor, and kids risk getting caught mid-sneak.

C06.why: The core action is tapping hay and placing conveyors to watch numbers go up; the 'needle found' moment is a lottery outcome not a skill or decision, so there is nothing fun here once progression is removed.
C06.fix: Only salvage is to change the core verb: make needle-finding an active physical search (dig, dive, metal-detect minigame in the pile with competitive player interference) rather than an automation incremental.

C07.why: Shared-fate tether is proven comedy (Chained Together, PEAK) and anchoring a dangling friend is a great clutch moment, but with random strangers one weak or leaving climber makes failure frustrating instead of funny, and physics climbing on touch controls is fragile.
C07.fix: Add a stranger-safe layer: auto re-tether/drop-out handling when someone leaves, a limited 'cut rope' vote, and short pitches between campsites so a fall costs 60 s not 10 min.

C08.why: Co-op haunted exploration with bait/cameraman roles is solid, but Content Warning's magic is rewatching real footage of your friends screaming; a montage of server-side tags loses that and becomes a score screen.
C08.fix: Record actual character CFrames/animations and ghost events and replay them as a real clip in the theatre (deaths and pratfalls included), so the payoff is genuine shared comedy, not a tally.

C09.why: Drawing a rune and seeing lightning come out is tactile and immediately satisfying on touch, with real skill expression and emergent cross-player combos; risks are recognition misfires (frustrating failure) and 10-minute wave defence getting samey.
C09.fix: Use forgiving recognition with live trail preview and partial-power casts on sloppy shapes, and shorten runs to ~6 min with varied wave modifiers and objectives (escort, protect-the-ward) rather than pure hold-the-tower.

C10.why: Mutating lineage is a charming meta, but the minute-to-minute is placing pieces and watching auto-battles; the fun lives mostly in the progression/breeding layer, and the first 30 s is menu picking.
C10.fix: Give the player a live in-battle input (a tap ability or swap per round) and make mutations mechanically loud and weird (extra legs that change attack patterns, explode on death) so runs produce stories, not stat bumps.

C11.why: Noise-hunting entity plus encumbered loot carry creates natural tension, greed decisions and funny-scary caught moments that work with silent strangers; liminal settings risk feeling empty and samey without strong set pieces.
C11.fix: Make artifacts physical and noisy with weird properties (one hums, one floats, one screams when dropped) so every carry is a decision and accidents become stories.

C12.why: Role-split crisis has proven appeal, but 'engineer taps panels' and 'navigator pings a map' are menu jobs, and the pilot is bottlenecked by pings from strangers; fun is uneven across roles.
C12.fix: Make the engineer and navigator physically run around the cabin (extinguish fires, patch holes, crank landing gear Overcooked-style) and rotate roles mid-flight so nobody is stuck in the dull seat.

C13.why: OpenFront-style expansion has many real decisions and dramatic betrayals, but early elimination in a 15-minute match is brutal for kids, alliances without chat are thin, and the first 30 s is a map of pixels.
C13.fix: Eliminated players respawn as a rebel/minor faction in a frontier zone or become mercenaries, and add ping-based alliance offers with visible trust/betrayal states.

C14.why: A floating value meter dropping on every bump makes physics failure readable and funny, co-carry and door-holding work with strangers without chat, and each delivery is a short self-contained challenge; driving with on-screen pedals is the weak link.
C14.fix: Make the van ride itself part of the puzzle (parcels slide and must be strapped or held during turns) and keep routes short so carrying, not driving, dominates.

C15.why: Shared-conveyor drafting and merge-3 give dense decisions in a short loop, but half the time is spent watching auto-fights and being knocked out early in an 8-player elimination leaves players idle.
C15.fix: Add a contested draft (snatching from the same conveyor in real time) and let eliminated players become 'toy gremlins' who drop hazards onto remaining boards or bet on outcomes.

C16.why: Timed chores with chaos events is a generic Overcooked-lite; the concept is underspecified and the pets are framed as task generators rather than mischievous agents worth playing with.
C16.fix: Make each pet a physics-driven AI with a personality and escalating schemes (the parrot steals keys, the goat eats the curtains) so chasing and outsmarting pets is the core verb, not ticking chore boxes.

C17.why: Stacking tension and tower collapses are satisfying and funny, but turn-taking creates downtime and one careless stranger can wreck the team tower, which feels unfair rather than funny in co-op.
C17.fix: Use simultaneous placement (multiple cranes, everyone drops at once) and in versus add Tricky-Towers-style spells/sabotage so every player is acting every second.

C18.why: Gathering food, voting and training are chores whose payoff is a weekly battle players don't directly control; there is no satisfying moment-to-moment verb and individual agency is diluted across a whole server.
C18.fix: Only a different core would help: let players physically pilot body parts of the kaiju in live battles (one arm each, Raft-Rush-style) so the week of raising leads to a playable fight.

C19.why: Freeze-in-the-beam is instantly understandable, tense and funny, pranking gives agency, and it works perfectly without chat; the genre is crowded and the Guard's fun depends on good tools.
C19.fix: Give statues a pose-match freeze (you must strike the pose you were placed in, sloppy poses are a tell) and give the Guard varied gadgets so both roles have skill expression.

C20.why: Short skill-based matches are fun without any progression and one-touch tapping is mobile-friendly, but 'tap where the ball goes' risks a low skill ceiling, and the pitch lacks any hook beyond the core sport.
C20.fix: Add timing windows (perfect set/spike quality, block timing) and movement/positioning decisions so rallies have skill depth and readable outplays.

overall_notes: Strongest pure-fun concepts are those whose core verb is funny or tense in the first 30 seconds and survives silent strangers: C05 Mom's Home (8), then C07, C09, C11, C14, C19 (7). Vetoes: C06 The Haystack and C18 Kaiju Keepers, whose core loops are progression/chores with no satisfying moment-to-moment verb. Watch-outs: C02 and C12 depend on coordination bandwidth that ping/emote-only strangers don't have; C10, C15 and C13 lean on watching or on progression for fun; C01 and C04 decay into memorization once content is learned. Several concepts (C08 montage, C03 single-button) undercut their own best moment and should fix that before production.
